label: First step on a fixed subset of tokens, plus first copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Two clauses, both tied to the start of a phase. (1) At t=0 the unit fires every time the first input is one of a c d g i j l p q s t u v w y 2 3, and never for the other 13 tokens. This covers about 89% of activations and 72% of the mass. The magnitude is small and set by the token alone, since h0 is fixed (c, q, t, i give the largest values). (2) At the second copy step (recall_idx=1, where the input is orig(0) fed back after <DEL>), it fires strongly in length-3 sequences. These are the top activations, up to the max of 0.234. In L=4 sequences it fires on about 30% of second copy steps, and I could not predict which ones from the tokens. It fires rarely for L>=5. It is essentially silent at t>=1 of the original phase, on <DEL>, and on later copy steps.

issues: The label says 'first copy step of length-3 sequences', but the predicate uses recall_idx==1. That is the SECOND output step: recall_idx 0 is the <DEL> step, and recall_idx 1 is the first step whose input is the fed-back orig(0). The explanation says 'second copy step' correctly, so the label contradicts the predicate and the explanation.

There is a systematic, coherent class of misses that the predicate does not capture: the second copy step of L=4 sequences (t==L+1, L==4). It fires on 30% of those steps (precision 0.30 dev) and holds about 11.8% of all activation mass, which is almost all of the test-split missed mass (11.8%). Its activations are among the larger ones (for example 0.28 and 0.45 relative to max in the misses output). The explanation discloses it, but the label leaves it out entirely.

I could not find a token-level predictor for the L=4 firing. I tried first_tok in the t=0 token set, digits and vowels in each orig position, n_digits, repeats, and the order of orig(1) and orig(3) relative to orig(0). All gave precision between 0.25 and 0.44. So about 12% of the mass stays unexplained, and the L=4 behavior looks like a graded continuation of the L=3 effect rather than a separate rule.

The claims that check out: t=0 & token-set has precision 1.0 and covers 88.8% of activations and 71.5% of mass. The complementary 13 tokens at t=0 never fire (precision 0). L=3 recall_idx==1 has precision 0.93. L>=5 recall_idx==1 is essentially silent (precision 0.0004). Original-phase t>=1 is silent (precision 0.0006). <DEL> has 10 of about 100k active. Test scores reproduce: precision 0.996, recall 0.927, F1 0.960, mass recall 0.882.
Extending to L<=4 gives test F1 0.921, precision 0.858, mass recall 0.998. That trades precision for the missing mass, so it is not a strictly better predicate under F1.
skeptic.revised_label: First input step on a fixed set of 17 tokens (weak, set by the token), plus the second copy step (input = fed-back orig(0)) of short sequences: reliably for L=3, on about 30% of L=4 sequences in a way that is not token-predictable (about 12% of mass unexplained)
